purpose: FR-A7 integration story (is_integration_story: true, owning_module intentionally omitted). Verifies — via table-driven property/interleaving tests against S3's REAL, already-landed producers — the four whole-flow guarantees architecture.md §6 'Order-Sensitive Composition' names for the inbound-application-rumor-ingest-and-authenticate flow (AC-ORDER-1..4). Owns no production code; a genuine gap found here is a defect against S2/S3, not new S4 scope.
dependencies_allowed: epochResolver (app/src/lib/marmot/epochResolver.ts) — real EpochResolver class, never mocked
dependencies_allowed_derivation: Union of the 'Spans modules:' lines on this story's 4 owned ACs in acceptance-criteria.md: AC-ORDER-1 -> {applicationRumorDispatcher, welcomeSubscription}, AC-ORDER-2 -> {EpochResolver, welcomeSubscription}, AC-ORDER-3 -> {EpochResolver, applicationRumorDispatcher}, AC-ORDER-4 -> {EpochResolver, welcomeSubscription, applicationRumorDispatcher}. Union = {applicationRumorDispatcher, epochResolver/EpochResolver, welcomeSubscription} — exactly the 3 files listed above. Corroborated against, not sourced from, architecture.md's broader '## Order-Sensitive Composition' participating-modules list, which additionally names 'chatPersistence / handlers' as a candidate whole-flow guarantee surface that did NOT survive into any of the 4 owned ACs' 'Spans modules:' lines — per Step 1's carve-out instruction, chatPersistence/handlers is therefore correctly excluded from this story's dependencies_allowed.
dependencies_forbidden: Any production-code edit to applicationRumorDispatcher.ts, epochResolver.ts, or welcomeSubscription.ts — this is a verification-only story (scope.excludes: 'Any new production behavior'); a diff to any of these three files would be an S2/S3 defect fix mis-scoped into S4, not S4 work

Mocking/stubbing applicationRumorDispatcher, EpochResolver, or welcomeSubscription's subscribeToGroupMessages — FR-A7's Mock Strategy exception requires these to be exercised for real; only the external marmot-ts codec (deserializeApplicationData/serializeClientState/deserializeClientState/getEpoch/getGroupMembers) and the NDK/relay transport boundary may be faked
external_ports: @internet-privacy/marmot-ts (fake codec boundary — deserializeApplicationData, serializeClientState, deserializeClientState, getEpoch, getGroupMembers; mirrors the established pattern in epochResolver.test.ts)
@nostr-dev-kit/ndk (fake NDKRelaySet.fromRelayUrls only, via importOriginal — mirrors welcomeSubscription.test.ts)
@/src/lib/pendingInvitations (stubbed — imported by welcomeSubscription.ts at module scope for unrelated exports, not exercised by subscribeToGroupMessages)

test_design_decisions.property_framework: fast-check is NOT a devDependency of app/ (confirmed via grep of package.json and package-lock.json) and this story does not add one, per the brief's instruction. Orderings/interleavings are generated by hand via a small in-file permutations<T>() helper, fed through vitest's table-driven it.each — the established project convention (chatPersistence.test.ts and parseStructured.contract.test.ts both cite 'table-driven it.each per project convention' explicitly as the fast-check substitute). Sufficient for the small (3-4 element) state spaces AC-ORDER-1..4 name.
test_design_decisions.fake_boundary_rationale: The dispatcher's MarmotGroupLike (on/off for authenticatedApplicationMessage/unauthenticatedMessage) and EpochResolver's MlsGroupLike (state/ingest/save) are BOTH implemented by one fake object (makeCombinedFakeGroup) mirroring production's single MarmotGroup instance serving both roles. Its scripted ingest() ALSO fires the corresponding group-level event synchronously before yielding its IngestResult, modeling the S3-confirmed fact (S3 result.json: 'applicationMessage (:1079/:1298) and authenticatedApplicationMessage (:1080/:1299) fire from identical adjacent lines') that both channels originate from the same underlying library processing. This is the legitimate external-library boundary named in the brief ('a fake underlying MLS group / fake MlsGroupLike'), not a mock of any module under test.
test_design_decisions.welcomeSubscription_boundary: subscribeToGroupMessages is driven for REAL (never mocked) via the same fake-NDK harness pattern welcomeSubscription.test.ts already established (mock ndkClient.fetchEventsWithTimeout for the historical phase; mock NDKRelaySet via importOriginal; a fake ndk.subscribe() capturing the live handler) — EXCEPT this file does NOT mock @/src/lib/marmot/epochResolver, unlike that existing file, since EpochResolver is a producer under test here, not an incidental dependency to silence.
test_design_decisions.welcomeSubscription_module_singleton_cav: welcomeSubscription.ts's seenIdsByGroup Map is module-level (shared across the whole test process, never reset). Every test uses a crypto.randomUUID()-suffixed groupId to guarantee isolation, mirroring the existing welcomeSubscription.test.ts convention (distinct group ids per test).
test_design_decisions.ac_order_1_scoping: AC-ORDER-1 is tested twice: (a) a dispatcher-only exhaustive 6-permutation test isolating applicationRumorDispatcher.ts's rumor-id LRU in the most literal reading of 'a sender-mismatched rumor sharing the same rumor id' (both legitimate and mismatched decode to the identical inner rumor.id); (b) a combined welcomeSubscription+dispatcher 6-permutation test proving welcomeSubscription's independent raw-event-id dedup set is not cross-poisoned, using DISTINCT raw/outer event ids (as two real raw kind-445 events necessarily would be) that BOTH decode to the shared inner rumor id. Historical/live channel-crossing for AC-ORDER-1's scenario is not separately re-permuted in (b) — that crossing is covered by the dedicated AC-ORDER-4 tests below, which test the same dedup mechanism from the channel-overlap angle; duplicating the full historical x live x ordering cross-product here was judged disproportionate to the incremental signal.
test_design_decisions.ac_order_3_scoping: Tests replay COUNT (1, 2, 3 competing-commit rollback cycles) as the primary 'independent of replay order/count' axis, comparing dispatcher-delivered call counts between a resolver with onApplicationMessage wired vs one matching welcomeSubscription.ts's actual production construction (callback omitted). Does not additionally permute the internal ordering of multiple queued replay-window messages within a single cycle — that ordering is fixed by insertion (FIFO into replayQueue) in the real code, not a free variable, so permuting it would not exercise a different code path.
test_design_decisions.adversarial_falsification_addendum: One constructed (not generated) adversarial case was attempted per FR-A7's addendum, chosen from the addendum's own example list ('crash-recovery split points'): a raw event lands in EpochResolver's future-epoch buffer (unreadable, never resolved) and the subscription is torn down (dispose()) before any resolving commit arrives; a FRESH post-crash subscribeToGroupMessages instance for the same group must still be able to re-ingest it. Reproduced against the real, already-landed S3 code: the guarantee HOLDS (test passes) — no finding to report. Added as a deterministic regression test alongside the generative permutation tests, per the addendum's instruction.

non_tautology_verification: Per VQ-S4-004/pre-impl question, two of the four guarantees were falsified by hand against the REAL production files before finalizing: (1) applicationRumorDispatcher.ts — moved markSeen() to fire BEFORE the choke-point drop instead of after; exactly the 2 'mismatched-first' orderings (of 6) in the AC-ORDER-1 dispatcher-layer test failed, all others still passed, confirming the test is order-sensitive and state-discriminating, not a tautology. (2) epochResolver.ts — changed the 'rejected' branch in processEvent to push onto futureBuffer like 'unreadable' instead of no-op; all 28 AC-ORDER-2 permutation/interleaving tests failed. Both mutations were reverted immediately after observing the expected failures (verified via diff against a pre-mutation backup); the working tree is unchanged from before this verification pass.
